subject: Next steps: Reserved capacity benchmarks & scope (Atlas Health)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Desai <maya@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-06T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up & proposed benchmark scope from today's call

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and a practical proposal for the competitive bench/tests you asked for comparing Reserved (Redwood Dedicated) vs hyperscaler GPU offerings. High-level takeaways from the call:

- You want predictable latency and unit cost at production scale for our clinical summarization workload (avg 400 tokens, p95 target <= 250ms).
- Procurement needs clear commitment options and failure-remediation language (penalties/credits).
- Security and auditability (audit logs, KMS integration) are gating items for legal.

Proposed evaluation scope (recommended, 7–10 business days):
1) Reserved-capacity trial: provision a dedicated pool equivalent to 16x A100s (or closest match) for 10 business days with pinned capacity and a simple SLA (p95 latency & availability). We'll run your model and an open baseline (Llama-2-Chat / running quantized) for apples-to-apples.
2) Throughput & latency benchmarking: coordinated runs at 50%, 75%, and 100% of target request rates; measure p50/p95/p99 for 256/512/1024 context lengths.
3) Failover & routing: controlled outage simulated on the dedicated pool; validate automatic routing to fallback models (regional hyperscaler endpoint) and observe impact on latency and tokens consumed.
4) Cost modeling: effective cost per 1k tokens at observed throughput for both reserved and hyperscaler options (including network egress when applicable).
5) Security checklist: SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM integration proof, and audit log sample export.

Deliverables we'll provide:
- Test matrix and runbook (detailed steps + required Atlas Health inputs)
- Collated benchmark results and a short analysis deck
- Draft SLA and reserved-commitment terms for procurement

Next steps I propose:
- Please confirm the scope and the two-week window you'd prefer to run tests (we can start as early as July 13).
- Add your procurement contact (if not Evan, please share) so we can send the SLA draft and pricing.

I've attached a short slide deck that highlights the differences in routing, caching, and failure modes between our Dedicated offering and typical hyperscaler reserved/spot mixes.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-hyperscaler-slide-deck.pdf (slide highlights)

Thanks — looking forward to aligning on dates.

— Jordan

Subject: Re: Follow-up & proposed benchmark scope from today's call

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications before we lock dates:

1) For the reserved-capacity trial, what are the minimum-term and cancellation terms? We need to understand if there's a daily proration or early-termination charge.
2) Can you give a ballpark of expected cost per 1k tokens for the reserved pool (just a rough figure so procurement has a reference)?
3) For the failover test, will Redwood simulate the hyperscaler side or do we need to provide an endpoint?

Evan (cc'd) is our procurement/ops lead — he'll own the SLA review.

— Maya
Maya Desai
Director, ML Platforms
Atlas Health
maya@atlashealth.ai
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Desai <maya@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Evan Ross <evan.ross@atlashealth.ai>
Date: 2026-07-06T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & proposed benchmark scope from today's call

Maya / Evan —

Great questions, answered inline below. I've attached a short SLA draft and a pricing summary for reference.

1) Minimum-term / cancellation:
- Option A (short trial): 10 business days reserved with daily proration and no early-termination fee (trial-only).
- Option B (monthly reserved): 1-month minimum, prorated by day after the first 30 days; early termination carries a 20% of remaining monthly commitment as a fee (this is negotiable for enterprise accounts).

2) Ballpark cost per 1k tokens (reserved pool, observed at 75% utilization):
- Dedicated (Redwood): ~$0.85 – $1.10 per 1k tokens (depends on quantization & batching).
- Hyperscaler (managed GPUs w/ preemptible options): ~$1.10 – $1.60 per 1k tokens (adds variability and egress).

Note: We'll produce a microcost model tied to your specific workload during the test window — those numbers are rough estimates.

3) Failover test details: we can simulate the hyperscaler fallback in two ways:
- A: Redwood will route traffic to our regional public endpoint that mimics a hyperscaler latency profile (fast to set up).
- B: Atlas provides a hyperscaler endpoint and we route test traffic there (preferred if you want real hyperscaler metrics).

Attachments included: sla-draft-AtlasHealth-2026.docx, redwood-dedicated-vs-hyperscaler-slide-deck.pdf

Action items I can take this week:
- Lock test start date (I propose July 13 — July 24).
- Circulate a one-page runbook with test matrix and the single-run checklist we need from your side (model weights or test harness endpoints).
- Marissa (cc) will follow up with more granular pricing options and any volume discounts.

Let me know if July 13 works and whether you want option A (Redwood-simulated hyperscaler) or option B (Atlas-provided endpoint) for failover.

— Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Ross <evan.ross@atlashealth.ai>, Maya Desai <maya@atlashealth.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-06T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing notes and commitment tiers

Hi Evan / Maya —

Looping in the pricing details quickly so procurement has something actionable. High-level tiers (subject to final SOW):

- Trial (no commitment): 10 business days, daily proration, no termination fee. Includes up to 2 TB ephemeral KV cache and standard support.
- Reserved 1-month: 30-day minimum, 20% early-termination fee if canceled before 30 days. Base discount 8% vs on-demand.
- Reserved 12-month: Annual commit, negotiated discounts (15–25% depending on committed vCPU/GPU hours and committed throughput). Includes prioritized capacity and 24/7 enterprise support SLA.

We can also include a contractual credit for missed availability (standard uptime credit schedule) and an ops-runbook addendum for failover steps. I'll attach the SLA draft Jordan circulated and can produce a short cost table that maps your expected RPS to effective $/1k tokens per tier.

Attachments: sla-draft-AtlasHealth-2026.docx

— Marissa
